mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction that triggers equity sell-offs, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC for interaction term over any 2-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) during supply chain disruptions reduces manufacturing output and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 105.0, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained employment growth above 100,000 monthly additions (PAYEMS > 100,000) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS > 100,000, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index level above 250 indicates elevated inflation that may trigger monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 250, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate decline (FEDFUNDS) and money supply increase (RSAFS) indicate aggressive monetary easing that boosts equity valuations, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through liquidity-driven price appreciation.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines and RSAFS increases, or Rank IC for interaction term over any 2-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), weak employment growth (PAYEMS < 100,000) indicates insufficient job creation to support consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS < 100,000, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window remains below 0.03.
